skill.name: psp-signal-hunt

skill.summary: Create a ranked, operational hunt list for timely ICP buying signals.

content.value_statement: Teams often lack a consistent way to identify timely buying signals for a specific ICP segment. This skill creates a ranked hunt list with sources, cadence, freshness rules, and implied pain.
actual_capabilities: Accepts a defined ICP segment and requests more precision when the segment is vague.
Generates 5-10 candidates across hiring, funding, leadership, product, pivot, and content signals.
Specifies what to look for, where to find it, and how often to monitor it.
Ranks candidates by volume, specificity, and operational effort.
Formats results as a Markdown table with a recommended hunt stack and freshness notes.
limitations: It does not fetch or verify live signal data; it defines signals and sources to monitor.
It requires a specific ICP segment for useful recommendations.
It does not automate LinkedIn, Crunchbase, RSS, or third-party data collection.
Its pain implications are hypotheses that require human validation.

use_cases.title: Build a Sales Signal Queue
use_cases.description: Sales operations teams can define repeatable signals, monitoring sources, cadences, and freshness rules for target accounts.

use_cases.title: Plan Market Research
use_cases.description: Market researchers can compare signal categories and rank research efforts by volume, specificity, and operational effort.

use_cases.title: Focus Founder Outreach
use_cases.description: Founders can identify timely public events that may indicate operational pain for a narrowly defined customer segment.

prompt_templates.title: Start with an ICP
prompt_templates.prompt: For this ICP, list 5 public signals worth tracking: Series B SaaS companies, $20-50M ARR, product-led growth.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a basic signal list.

prompt_templates.title: Add Monitoring Details
prompt_templates.prompt: For Series B SaaS companies with $20-50M ARR and a product-led motion, give 8 signals with what to look for, sources, cadence, and implied pain.

prompt_templates.title: Rank the Hunt
prompt_templates.prompt: For US-based fintech companies hiring their first revenue operations leader, generate 10 signals and rank them by monthly volume, specificity, and monitoring effort.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prioritize signals for a defined segment.

prompt_templates.title: Design the Full System
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a signal-hunting system for European B2B cybersecurity companies after a funding round. Include 10 ranked signals, sources, cadence, freshness limits, implied pain, and handoff notes for outreach.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for an outreach workflow.

output_examples.input: ICP: Series B SaaS companies with $20-50M ARR and a product-led growth motion.
output: Hiring: Demand Generation Lead posted within 14 days; source: LinkedIn job search and RSS; cadence: daily; implied pain: pipeline gap.
Funding: Series B announcement within 30 days; source: Crunchbase and company news; cadence: weekly; implied pain: pressure to accelerate growth.
Product: New pricing tier within 45 days; source: pricing pages and release notes; cadence: weekly; implied pain: monetization or packaging work.

output_examples.input: ICP: US fintech companies hiring their first revenue operations leader.
output_examples.output: The strongest starting signal is a new revenue operations leadership role. Monitor company job pages weekly, capture the posting date, and remove the signal after 45 days unless refreshed.

best_practices: Define company stage, revenue range, motion, and geography before hunting.
Attach a freshness window and capture date to every signal.
Validate implied pain before using a signal in outreach.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague ICP descriptions such as technology companies.
Do not treat a public event as proof of active buying intent.
Do not keep stale signals in an outreach queue.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces 5-10 ranked public signals with search locations, monitoring cadence, and implied operational pain.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide a specific ICP with company type, stage, revenue range, business motion, geography, or similar constraints.

faq.question: Does it collect live data?
faq.answer: No. It defines signals and recommends sources, but it does not retrieve or verify current events.

faq.question: Which signal categories are supported?
faq.answer: The categories are hiring, funding, leadership, product, pivot, and content.

faq.question: How are signals prioritized?
faq.answer: Signals are ranked by expected volume, specificity to actionable pain, and operational effort.

faq.question: Can I use the results for outreach?
faq.answer: Yes, after checking the source, capture date, freshness window, and whether the implied pain is supported.
